briefing: 今日导读：OpenAI在欧盟引入文本水印，确保AI生成内容的可追溯性；Reflection推出Beam开源AI模型，挑战中国市场；Hinton发布AI领域新兴论文，探索技术前沿。这些事件展现了AI行业在合规性和技术创新上的动态。
highlights: 今日看点：OpenAI在欧盟添加文本水印引发关于AI合规性的讨论，与此同时，Reflection的Beam开源模型则标志着全球AI技术的竞争加剧。这两个事件反映出AI技术在法律合规和市场竞争方面的双重压力。Hinton的新论文则进一步推动了AI技术的基础研究，揭示出行业在不断寻找创新突破口。整体来看，当前AI行业正处于技术快速演进和合规压力交织的阶段。

events.title: OpenAI 在欧盟实施文本水印
events.summary: OpenAI将在欧盟为ChatGPT和Codex添加文本水印，以遵守AI法案。该水印为无形、机器可读，OpenAI表示其textGrain水印的效果匹配或超过了其他方案，如Google DeepMind的SynthID。
events.insight:
### 一句话本质
OpenAI在欧盟的ChatGPT和Codex实现无形文本水印，确保生成内容的可追溯性。

### 为什么令人兴奋
这表示从未尝试的合规性技术进入实用阶段，可能立竿见影地改变合规和溯源问题处理。

### 产品机会
AI合规模块和审计工具推动生成性AI进军受到合规要求的领域，如医疗和金融。

### 格局影响
强化了OpenAI在合规性技术上的领先地位，对其他公司构成技术压力和法规遵循的竞争力。

### 冷静判断
水印需在多种场景下测试才能证明其真正价值，对普通开发者的应用可能需要具体支持和开发文档。

### 趋势坐标
合规性和透明性成为AI行业发展的重要加速器，与近期全球对AI法规的重视呼应。

articles.text: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act. Editing can make the invisible marks harder to detect, it says.

articles.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
articles.text: An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first. OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August . Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act ; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition. OpenAI also included scores from AI benchmarks showing similar performance from watermarked and unwatermarked text. events.title: AI 对数学的冲击与争议
events.summary: 过去一年，OpenAI、Anthropic等实验室在多个长期数学问题上取得突破，甚至解决了著名的千年奖提案之一。尽管取得了重大的进展，但这些成果引发了学术界的 backlash，OpenAI则表示会向精英数学家咨询，避免再次犯错。

articles.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
articles.text: This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things , barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer . Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash . AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen. Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics. articles.title: Sen. Adam Schiff on AI regulation, free speech, and impeaching Trump one more time
articles.text: Today, I’m talking with Sen. Adam Schiff, a Democrat from California. Schiff sits on a number of committees with oversight into tech and AI: intellectual property, antitrust, privacy and technology — it’s all there. I really wanted to ask him about how we might regulate anything related to the tech industry at this moment in time. But as you’ll hear, he started our conversation by talking about the self-dealing and corruption present all through our politics. That of course fell against the backdrop of President Donald Trump gathering AI CEOs to the White House to sign a nonbinding pact in which they agree to, you know, do a good job keeping AI safe. I asked Schiff if he thinks that’s enough, how he thinks a more formal regulatory framework would look, and what might happen next if Democrats retake Congress in the midterms — all the way to whether he’d support impeaching the president ( again ) over all that corruption. We also spent some time comparing and contrasting how you might regulate AI with where we’ve landed regulating social media. One nerdy note: You’re going to hear me ask the senator about something called Chevron deference and a Supreme Court case called Loper Bright. Basically, the Supreme Court overturned a Reagan-era precedent saying courts would defer to experts in agencies when the law was vague. Now, the courts get to decide, which could cause any new regulation to get immediately tied up in litigation. That seems awfully relevant to the idea of creating a new agency to regulate AI, which Schiff supports doing. Okay: California Sen. Adam Schiff. Here we go. articles.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen, but AI is totally worth it
articles.text: Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way. The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.
